name: Passover
overview: The Passover, as instituted in Exodus 12, is a divinely ordained observance where each Israelite household selects a lamb without blemish on the tenth day of the month and keeps it until the fourteenth day when it is slain. The blood of the lamb is applied to the doorposts as a sign of protection, and the lamb is eaten that night with unleavened bread and bitter herbs, symbolizing deliverance and God's provision. This precise design underscores God's command for obedience and remembrance of His saving power.
